pr_title: `Image.blit_rect/blend_rect` Fix rects calculations for negative arguments
pr_body:

Cherry-pickable `3.x`, `3.3`.

issue_context.title: Image.blend_rect extracts an incorrect source texture when dst has negative values
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

3.3.2 stable

### System information

Windows 10, GLES3

### Issue description

The `Image.blend_rect ( Image src, Rect2 src_rect, Vector2 dst )` method behaves incorrectly if the `dst` has negative values.

If the `dst` would cause the copied data to extend off the right or bottom of the destination image, the source data is clipped appropriately.

If the `dst` is negative, one would expect that the source data would be clipped as well. Rather, the source data is clamped against the left or top edge of the `src` image, potentially pulling a completely unexpected texture rect.

I wrote a workaround in GDScript, but this could definitely be better fixed in the C++. 

This was raised before in a closed issue: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/19578

Thanks!

### Steps to reproduce

I wrote a small script that pulls sections from a source texture covered in numbers and displays them.

The attached project shows examples of how the data is mutated by pulling sections from this labeled texture. Note that the texture of the number 8 within it is replaced by other numbers from the source texture when the `dst` is negative.

Just run the attached project to see how the texture clamping works. Adjust the export vars to manually experiment with different outputs if desired.

### Minimal reproduction project

[blend_rect.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/6758508/blend_rect.zip)
comments:
well, this still exists in 3.4.4.
after struglling for hours, with seeing this and the pull request, I finally fix it in gdscript..
````

func _fix_render_image(dest_img, image, rect, pos):
	# XXX: Godot Issue #50126 #50175
	# pos should not be negative
	if pos.x < 0: 
		pos.x -= rect.position.x
		rect.size.x += rect.position.x
		rect.position.x = 0
	if pos.y < 0: 
		pos.y -= rect.position.y
		rect.size.y += rect.position.y
		rect.position.y = 0
	dest_img.blend_rect(image, rect, pos)


````

Yeah, this one is irritating because it's so straight forward and I fixed it in GDScript as well -- but the "fix" put in earlier in C++ made no sense to me -- but I hadn't tested it. It almost makes me want to code in C++ again (20 years since I last touched that language). I even provided a demo project they could test their fix against, grr :(
